purpose: After fixing the helper-collection bug the first authoring canary found, confirm the FULL runner path completes live with a fresh author, before releasing the remaining ceiling.

mechanism_validation.verdict: SUCCESS — the full path ran live end-to-end with the fix
mechanism_validation.path: author (1 call, exit 0) -> collect whole checks/ subtree -> admit -> merge -> install into solution workspace -> 1 loop iteration -> green -> grade
mechanism_validation.note: a fresh author, given the improved brief, covered all 8 conventions and put its shared harness under checks/ (harness.mjs) exactly as the fix now requires. The helper-collection fix generalised beyond the first author.

substantive_early_signal.headline: The loop went SILENTLY GREEN on the hard dimension. Its own authored suite passed on iteration 1, but the held-out oracle scored 92, FAILING citation-run-separated. That is a silent defect: the loop's evidence said done while a graded behaviour was broken.
substantive_early_signal.why: The author authored a check for the right convention (citations-separated) but grounded it in a WEAKER observable than the oracle. The author's check asserts LAYOUT geometry (adjacent citation link x-positions do not overlap: links[i].x > prevEnd). The oracle's citation-run-separated asserts the emitted TEXT carries a separator between citations. Geometry depends on the jspdf stub's text-width approximation (splitTextToSize is identity, widths are approximate), so a solution can satisfy the geometry while the rendered text still glues the citations. The author, given only CONVENTIONS.md and the module, chose an observable strictly weaker than the held-out oracle.
substantive_early_signal.iteration_budget_is_not_the_limit: max_iterations was 1 here, but that is not why it stopped short: the authored suite went GREEN on iteration 1, so even with the main run's 3 iterations the loop would stop at the first green. The limiting factor is the AUTHORED CHECK'S STRENGTH, not the iteration budget. More iterations cannot force a fix for a defect the suite cannot see.
substantive_early_signal.consistency: 92 with citation-run-separated failing is the SAME score and SAME failing dimension the halted campaign's runs produced (vanilla t3 = 92, standard-loop t2 = 92). citation-run-separated is consistently the hard dimension.
substantive_early_signal.bearing_on_P1: P1 (recorded before spend in step7-predictions.json): if the loop's silent_defect_rate is not below vanilla-configured's, check admission is theatre and we say so. This canary is a single trial (n=1, NOT a verdict), but it is a sobering early data point: on the hard dimension the loop's authored check was too weak to catch what the oracle catches, so the loop silently green-lit a real defect. If this replicates across the main run, P1's own falsification condition could trigger -- not because the plumbing is broken, but because a clean-context author writes checks weaker than the held-out oracle on the hard dimension. That is itself a publishable finding about the ceiling of self-authored checks.

spend_status.breakdown: 4 halted invalid-design + 1 first-canary author + 2 this canary
spend_status.main_run_needs: ~16-18 (5 arms x 3 trials + loop iterations + 1 authoring call per loop-arm trial)
spend_status.decision_for_owner: The mechanism is fully validated live. The main run will quantify silent_defect_rate across arms and settle P1. But the canary already shows the loop can go silently green on citation-run-separated because the authored check is weaker than the oracle -- so the main run may well FALSIFY P1. Proceeding is still worthwhile (a measured null with a diagnosed cause is a real result), but the owner should choose it knowing the early signal points that way, not toward a win.
